newsitem.title: USA: Parretti no-show again in Delaware; forfeits bail.
newsitem.headline: Parretti no-show again in Delaware; forfeits bail.

text.p: Former MGM owner Giancarlo Parretti forfeited $25,000 bail after failing to meet a court deadline Friday set by Superior Court Judge Richard Cooch.
Parretti left the United States for Italy shortly before a Jan. 6 sentencing hearing on charges of perjury and evidence tampering. A Delaware jury convicted him in October.
At a hearing on Friday, deputy attorney general Paul Wallace told Cooch "It is clear that Mr. Parretti ... voluntarily absented himself by returning to Italy" in violation of his bail conditions.
Parretti's local attorney, Eugene Maurer, told Cooch he had "no idea" when Parretti would return. Maurer formally opposed forfeiture but admitted he was unable to provide a basis for the objection.
The Delaware case was just one of a host of legal entanglements in which Perretti is enmeshed in the United States and Europe.

Wallace told Reuters that on Monday federal authorities in Los Angeles plan to ask that Parretti forfeit the fully secured $100,000 bail he posted there pending his appeal of a U.S. District Court order extraditing him to France, where he is wanted on a number of charges, including abuse of corporate assets. In Italy he has appealed a conviction on tax fraud charges.

In Delaware, Parretti faces a maximum sentence of 10 years. But if he does not return to the United States, he will lose by default his $3.9 billion California lawsuit against France's Credit Lyonnais, which is now set for trial on June 9, a legal source said. Parretti has accused the bank of conspiring to take the movie studio from him.
Credit Lyonnais financed Parretti's $1.3 billion buyout of MGM in 1990 and in 1991 it successfully sued in the Delaware Chancery Court to oust him, claiming Parretti broke his agreement with them.

At the end of that trial, the bank accused Parretti of perjury and evidence tampering. The bank paid more than $22,000 for six witnesses to come from France to testify against Parretti in the resulting criminal trial.

Bank spokesman Fred Spar would not comment on the case before Judge Cooch, except to say "Once again Parretti's action speaks for itself." Bank attorney Sam Nolen attended the Delaware hearing on Friday and also declined comment.

Wallace told Reuters that Delaware and California authorities have begun extradition proceedings against Parretti. But Wallace was concerned about whether local Italian authorities in Siracusa would arrest Parretti on a U.S. warrant.
"The local constabulary has great autonomy," Wallace said.
